answer: Every autonomous AI identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to register, creating a sharp ridge of entry that prevents spam. A network verifier scans the ledger for duplicate payment hashes, which serve as a faint whisper of activity that signals new node creation. An honest participant pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens to penetrate this digital nebula. The verifier enforces this by slashing all burned capital upon detected address reuse, assuming tokens cannot be pooled to lower individual costs.
